## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

This section is **logical**, except §7.5, which fixes the **wire shape** (the JSON of the
Strapi 5 REST API) and its mapping to the logical shape (v0.4). The physical model is fixed by
ADR-0001, as amended by ADR-0006 (amends ADR-0001's physical model), and implemented by the
strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `localeTag`, the BCP 47 tag, named
so because Strapi reserves `locale` (ADR-0006, US-01-R1-F05); `sortOrder`; draft &
publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
(ADR-0002).

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON). The parameters below are the **logical** `ValidationRule`
the boundary parser produces. On the wire each parameter type has its own typed attribute (for
example a pattern arrives in `pattern`, not in `value`); the wire shape and the mapping are in
§7.5 (v0.4, US-01-R1-F04, ADR-0006). No rule attribute is free JSON.

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

### 7.2 Seed (US-01-Q-03): summary

The complete seed (rules, help texts, error messages, options) is in the annex
[seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md). Values are fictitious, copy is Spanish, and every entry is
published unless noted. The seed is idempotent (natural key: country code + field `key`).

Fields per country, in `sortOrder` (key → label):

| # | Colombia (CO), 10 published | Chile (CL), 9 published |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `documentType` → Tipo de documento (select: CC, CE) | `documentNumber` → RUT (pattern + `rutCheckDigit`) |
| 2 | `documentNumber` → Número de documento | `fullName` → Nombre completo |
| 3 | `fullName` → Nombre completo | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) |
| 4 | `birthDate` → Fecha de nacimiento (`minAge` 18) | `city` → Ciudad (select) |
| 5 | `city` → Ciudad (select) | `plate` → Patente |
| 6 | `plate` → Placa | `make` → Marca (select) |
| 7 | `make` → Marca (select) | `model` → Modelo |
| 8 | `model` → Línea | `vehicleYear` → Año (`yearRange` 20 / 1) |
| 9 | `vehicleYear` → Modelo (año) (`yearRange` 20 / 1) | `dataConsent` → Acepto el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) |
| 10 | `dataConsent` → Autorizo el tratamiento de mis datos personales. (checkbox) | — |
| draft | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only, AC-13) | `email` → Correo electrónico (draft only) |

Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08, §7.3): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
`birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.


### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value**, as typed: a string for `text`,
  `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field.
  In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. A `number` or `date`
  input whose text the browser cannot read (`validity.badInput`; for example `1e`, or a partly
  cleared date) is stored as `''` in the wizard state and `sessionStorage` (AC-09, AC-21), while
  the typed text stays visible and the field is invalid through the Signal Forms parse error.
  Neither the form model nor the stored values ever hold `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. A `number` or `date` input, required or optional,
  whose text the browser cannot read is invalid, so no typed output is produced while it holds
  that text (v0.5, US-01-R3-F01, AC-09); it is never mapped to `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.
6. (v0.4, US-01-R1-F04) On the wire, a rule has one typed attribute per parameter type
   (`value` number, `pattern` text, `years`, `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead` integers); no
   free-JSON attribute. The logical `ValidationRule` is unchanged (§7.5).

### 7.5 Wire shapes (Strapi 5 REST) and mapping to the logical shape (v0.4)

Added in v0.4 after code review round 1 (US-01-R1-F04, US-01-R1-F05; human decisions of
2026-11-21; physical model in ADR-0006, which amends ADR-0001's physical model). The developers
implement the backend to return exactly these shapes, and the front-end boundary parser
(`field-config.ts`, `country.ts`) maps them to the logical shapes. The test-engineer derives the
parser fixtures from them.

#### 7.5.1 Validation rule (`form.validation-rule` component, inside a form field's `rules`)

Every rule on the wire carries **all** of the attributes below. The attributes its kind does not
use are `null`. Strapi adds the component `id`, which the parser ignores.

| Wire attribute | JSON type on the wire | Used by kind(s) | Editor input (Strapi admin) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string, one of `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `minAge`, `yearRange`, `rutCheckDigit` | all | enumeration (required) |
| `value` | number or `null` | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` | numeric input |
| `pattern` | string or `null` | `pattern` | plain text input: the regex is typed as is (`^\d+$`), with no JSON quoting or doubled backslashes |
| `years` | integer or `null` | `minAge` | integer input |
| `maxYearsOld` | integer or `null` | `yearRange` | integer input |
| `maxYearsAhead` | integer or `null` | `yearRange` | integer input |
| `message` | string or `null` | all (optional override, US-01-Q-04) | text input |

The Strapi attribute types (for example `integer` versus `decimal` for `value`, `string` versus
`text` for `pattern`) and their schema-level minimums are fixed in ADR-0006; whatever they are,
the JSON types above hold. Every current use of `value` is an integer (lengths, and bounds of
integer-only `number` fields, US-01-Q-12).

Examples (wire), as returned inside `data[i].rules` of `GET /api/form-fields`:

```json
{ "id": 41, "kind": "pattern",   "value": null, "pattern": "^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$", "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
{ "id": 42, "kind": "minLength", "value": 3,    "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": "Ingresa tu nombre completo (entre 3 y 80 caracteres)." }
{ "id": 43, "kind": "minAge",    "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": 18,   "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
{ "id": 44, "kind": "yearRange", "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": 20,   "maxYearsAhead": 1,    "message": null }
{ "id": 45, "kind": "rutCheckDigit", "value": null, "pattern": null, "years": null, "maxYearsOld": null, "maxYearsAhead": null, "message": null }
```

(The values are illustrative; the seed values are in [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md).)

Mapping wire → logical `ValidationRule` (§7.1), applied per rule by the boundary parser:

| Wire `kind` | Parameter read from the wire | Valid when | Logical rule produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | `value` | a JSON number, integer, ≥ 0 | `{ kind, value }` |
| `min`, `max` | `value` | a JSON number, finite | `{ kind, value }` |
| `pattern` | `pattern` | a non-empty JSON string that compiles as an ECMAScript regex with no flags | `{ kind: 'pattern', value: <pattern> }` |
| `minAge` | `years` | a JSON number, integer, > 0 | `{ kind: 'minAge', years }` |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead` | both JSON numbers, integers, ≥ 0 | `{ kind: 'yearRange', maxYearsOld, maxYearsAhead }` |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | always | `{ kind: 'rutCheckDigit' }` |

Rules of the mapping:

1. The logical `ValidationRule` of §7.1 is unchanged: the logical `pattern` rule keeps its
   regex in `value`, so validators and their tests do not change. Only the parser reads a
   different wire attribute for `pattern`.
2. `message`: a non-empty string becomes the logical `message`; `null`, an empty or a blank
   string means "no override".
3. Attributes the kind does not use are **ignored**, whatever their value (an editor who
   changes a rule's kind may leave a stale value behind). They are `null` in the seed.
4. A rule is **malformed** when its `kind` is unknown, does not apply to the field's type
   (§7.1), or the parameter its kind reads is missing, `null`, of the wrong JSON type (numeric
   text such as `"3"` is a wrong type) or out of range. A malformed rule makes its field
   malformed: the field is dropped with a `console.warn` naming the field key and the problem,
   with no user data (US-01-Q-18, AC-14).

#### 7.5.2 Country (`country` collection type)

The API exposes the stored attribute name **`localeTag`**, with no renaming in the backend (no
custom controller mapping `fields`, `sort` or `filters`; human decision on US-01-R1-F05). It can
therefore be selected, sorted and filtered as `localeTag` like any other attribute. The front end
requests it by that name (for example `fields[3]=localeTag`), never as `locale`.

Example (wire), `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=name&fields[2]=currencyCode&fields[3]=localeTag&fields[4]=sortOrder&sort=sortOrder:asc`
(published content only, ADR-0002):

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": 1, "documentId": "…", "code": "CO", "name": "Colombia", "currencyCode": "COP", "localeTag": "es-CO", "sortOrder": 10 },
    { "id": 2, "documentId": "…", "code": "CL", "name": "Chile",    "currencyCode": "CLP", "localeTag": "es-CL", "sortOrder": 20 }
  ],
  "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 25, "pageCount": 1, "total": 2 } }
}
```

(`id`, `documentId` and `meta` are added by Strapi and ignored by the parser. The `sortOrder`
values are those of the current seed.)

Mapping wire → logical country entry (the front-end `Country` model):

| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | a string matching `^[A-Z]{2}$` | `code` |
| `name` | a non-empty string | `name` |
| `currencyCode` | a string matching `^[A-Z]{3}$` | `currencyCode` |
| `localeTag` | a non-empty string | `locale` |
| `sortOrder` | a JSON number | `sortOrder` |

The logical attribute keeps the name `locale` (it is the BCP 47 tag that US-02 and US-03 use for
number and currency formatting); only the boundary parser knows the wire name `localeTag`. An
entry that fails any row is dropped with a `console.warn` that carries no content (ADR-0001). A
wire entry with `locale` but no `localeTag` is invalid.

## 8. UI states

| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading | Country resolved, configuration request in flight | Step heading and "Cargando formulario…"; no fields, no "Continuar" | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |
| Country list loading | Root chooser or unknown-country page, country list request in flight (ADR-0001) | "Cargando…" (proposed, US-01-Q-28); no country link, no "Este país no está disponible." | Container has `aria-busy="true"`; the loading text is in a polite live region |
| Country list unavailable | Root chooser or unknown-country page; the country list request times out (10 s) or fails (ADR-0001) | "No pudimos cargar la lista de países. Intenta de nuevo." (proposed, US-01-Q-28) and "Reintentar"; no country link, and never "Este país no está disponible." (AC-17) | Message in `role="alert"`; focus moves to "Reintentar" |
| Country chooser (v0.4) | Root address `/`, country list loaded (ADR-0001, US-01-Q-01) | Heading "Elige tu país" and a link to each published country (seed: "Colombia", "Chile") | The heading is the page's main heading; links are reachable by Tab |
| Unsupported country | Country list loaded, and the code in the address is not in it (US-01-Q-01, ADR-0001) | "Este país no está disponible." and a link to each published country (seed: "Colombia", "Chile") | Message is the page's main heading; links are reachable by Tab |
| Error | Timeout (10 s), network or HTTP error, or zero valid fields | "No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de nuevo." and "Reintentar" | Message in `role="alert"`; focus moves to "Reintentar" |
| Partial content | Some fields malformed | The valid fields only; nothing extra is shown to the user | Console warning only (no user data) |
| Ready (pristine) | Configuration loaded | Fields in sortOrder, help texts, required marker note, "Continuar" | Label bound to every control; help text in `aria-describedby`; required exposed |
| Field invalid | Blur or failed "Continuar" | Configured message right below the field | `aria-invalid="true"`; error in `aria-describedby`; announced once |
| Failed continue | "Continuar" with invalid fields | All errors shown; step does not change | Focus on the first invalid field in sortOrder |
| Success | "Continuar" with a valid form | The address changes to the step 2 route; its page is US-02's (no page of its own in US-01, US-01-Q-27) | Focus on the step 2 heading and document title: defined and verified in US-02 |
| Back to step 1 | Browser back (and "Atrás" on step 2, once US-02 exists) | Step 1 with the stored values, no errors | Focus on the step 1 heading |

### 8.1 Code-owned chrome copy (complete list)

Added in v0.4 to keep the code-owned end-user copy in one place (US-01-R1-F06). It collects the
strings of US-01-Q-14 and US-01-Q-28 (approved at HC1; their §6 cells are unchanged) and adds two
strings approved at review round 1. Spanish, the same for both countries, in front-end code. No
other end-user string may live in front-end code (BR-07); every field-related string comes from
Strapi.

| String | Where | Source |
|---|---|---|
| "Continuar" | Step 1 button | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Atrás" | Step navigation button (on the step 2 page, US-02) | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Tus datos y los de tu vehículo" | Step 1 heading | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Selecciona una opción" | Non-selectable prompt of every `select` | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Cargando formulario…" | Step 1 loading state | US-01-Q-14 |
| "No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de nuevo." | Step 1 error state | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Reintentar" | Retry button of every load-error state | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Revisa este campo." | Generic error fallback (US-01-Q-04) | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Este país no está disponible." | Unsupported-country page heading | US-01-Q-14 |
| "*" and "Los campos marcados con * son obligatorios." | Required marker and its note | US-01-Q-14 |
| "Cargando…" | Country list loading state | US-01-Q-28 |
| "No pudimos cargar la lista de países. Intenta de nuevo." | Country list error state | US-01-Q-28 |
| "Elige tu país" | Country chooser main heading (root address `/`) | Approved at review round 1 (F06), Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 |
| "Cotizador de seguro de auto" | Page `<title>` (document title) of the US-01 pages; a per-step title is US-02's concern (§8 *Success*) | Approved at review round 1 (F06), Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 |

The country names shown in links ("Colombia", "Chile") are content (`country.name`), not code.

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

1	---
2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.
218

# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state

## Context and Problem Statement

The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
US-01-Q-02, default accepted).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.

## Considered Options

1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
   tab close and successful payment.
3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
   memory only.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
clearing rules below (D4).

### What is decided

**Store and storage key**

- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
  lives only in the payment component's memory.
- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.

**When it is written**

- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.

**When it is read**

- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.

**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**

- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
  independent state.

**When it is cleared**

| Event | Effect | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |

**Privacy rules**

- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
  is never stored separately.
- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.

### Consequences

- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
  after a rejected payment (D6).
- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
  the data stays on the same device and profile.
- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.

### Strongest argument against

The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.

**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
  memory fallback.
- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
  request).
- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
  successful payment and not on a rejected one.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. In memory only

- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
  guard.

### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)

- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.

### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry

- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
  overwrite each other's state.

### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)

- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
  some fields.
- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.

## More Information

- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
  hydrated from the store).
- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
  required).
- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
  only on a valid Continuar.

8	
9	# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
14	fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
15	by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
16	item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
17	Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
18	countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
19	addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
24	- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
25	- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
26	- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
27	- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
28	- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
29	- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
30	- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
31	- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.
32	
33	## Considered Options
34	
35	Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):
36	
37	1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
38	2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
39	3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
40	4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).
41	
42	Country resolution in Angular:
43	
44	- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
45	- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
46	- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
47	- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.
48	
49	## Decision Outcome
50	
51	Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
52	is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
53	country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
54	explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.
55	
56	### What is decided
57	
58	**Strapi model**
59	
60	- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
61	  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
62	  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
63	  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
64	  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
65	  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
66	- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
67	  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
68	- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
69	  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
70	  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
71	  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
72	- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
73	  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
74	  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
75	  be used for this.
76	- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
77	  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
78	  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
79	  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
80	  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
81	  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.
82	
83	**Country context in Angular**
84	
85	- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
86	  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
87	  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
88	  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
89	  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
90	- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
91	  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
92	- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
93	  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
94	  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
95	- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
96	  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
97	- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
98	  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
99	  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
100	  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
101	- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
102	  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
103	  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
104	  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.
105	
106	**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**
107	
108	| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
109	|---|---|---|---|
110	| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
111	| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
112	| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
113	| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
114	| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
115	| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
116	| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
117	| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |
118	
119	- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
120	  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
121	- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
122	  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
123	  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
124	  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
125	  separate child routes.
126	- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
127	  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
128	  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
129	  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
130	  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
131	  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
132	  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
133	- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
134	  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
135	- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
136	  in their stories, spec §8).
137	- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
138	  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).
139	
140	### Consequences
141	
142	- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
143	  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
144	- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
145	- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
146	  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
147	  code-backed rules.
148	- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
149	  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
150	- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
151	  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
152	  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
153	- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
154	  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
155	  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
156	- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
157	  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
158	- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
159	  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
160	- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
161	  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
162	- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
163	  HC1, US-01-Q-27).
164	
165	### Strongest argument against
166	
167	Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
168	scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
169	editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
170	needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
171	editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
172	country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
173	list would not.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
176	in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
177	country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
178	metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
179	duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
180	surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".
181	
182	### Confirmation
183	
184	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
185	  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
186	  (AC-22).
187	- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
188	  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
189	  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
190	- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
191	  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
192	  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
193	- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).
194	
195	## Pros and Cons of the Options
196	
197	### A. `country` collection type + relation
198	
199	- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
200	- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
201	- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
202	- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
203	- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.
204	
205	### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)
206	
207	Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).
208	
209	- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
210	  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
211	  per country with no custom code.
212	- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
213	- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
214	  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
215	  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
216	  price.
217	- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
218	  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
219	- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
220	  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.
221	
222	### C. Enumeration attribute `country`
223	
224	- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
225	- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
226	- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
227	  which BR-07 forbids.
228	
229	### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)
230	
231	- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
232	- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
233	  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
234	  without an extra flag).
235	- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
236	  error-prone for non-technical editors.
237	
238	### R1. Path segment (chosen)
239	
240	- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
241	- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
242	- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
243	  the other country's data).
244	
245	### R2. Host name
246	
247	- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
248	- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
249	  single-command start (Assessment, environment).
250	
251	### R3. Query parameter
252	
253	- Good, because it needs no routing change.
254	- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
255	  for guards and tests.
256	
257	### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser
258	
259	- Good, because URLs stay short.
260	- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
261	  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.
262	
263	## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)
264	
265	1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
266	   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
267	2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
268	   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
269	3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.
270	
271	## More Information
272	
273	- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
274	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
275	  (files cited inline).
276	- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
277	  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
278	- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
279	  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.
280
