---
status: Accepted
date: 2026-11-20
decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, strapi-content-modeling skill, published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/i18n, @strapi/utils 5.63.0 and @angular/router 22.3.0
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
---

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

### Strongest argument against

Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
list would not.

**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
  (AC-22).
- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.

### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)

Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).

- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
  per country with no custom code.
- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
  price.
- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name

- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
  single-command start (Assessment, environment).

### R3. Query parameter

- Good, because it needs no routing change.
- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
  for guards and tests.

### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser

- Good, because URLs stay short.
- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.

## More Information

- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (files cited inline).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.

1	---
2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.

8	
9	# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
14	fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
15	by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
16	item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
17	Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
18	countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
19	addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
24	- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
25	- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
26	- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
27	- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
28	- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
29	- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
30	- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
31	- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.
32	
33	## Considered Options
34	
35	Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):
36	
37	1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
38	2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
39	3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
40	4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).
41	
42	Country resolution in Angular:
43	
44	- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
45	- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
46	- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
47	- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.
48	
49	## Decision Outcome
50	
51	Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
52	is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
53	country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
54	explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.
55	
56	### What is decided
57	
58	**Strapi model**
59	
60	- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
61	  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
62	  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
63	  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
64	  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
65	  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
66	- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
67	  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
68	- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
69	  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
70	  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
71	  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
72	- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
73	  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
74	  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
75	  be used for this.
76	- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
77	  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
78	  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
79	  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
80	  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
81	  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.
82	
83	**Country context in Angular**
84	
85	- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
86	  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
87	  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
88	  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
89	  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
90	- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
91	  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
92	- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
93	  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
94	  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
95	- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
96	  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
97	- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
98	  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
99	  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
100	  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
101	- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
102	  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
103	  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
104	  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.
105	
106	**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**
107	
108	| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
109	|---|---|---|---|
110	| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
111	| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
112	| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
113	| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
114	| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
115	| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
116	| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
117	| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |
118	
119	- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
120	  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
121	- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
122	  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
123	  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
124	  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
125	  separate child routes.
126	- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
127	  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
128	  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
129	  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
130	  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
131	  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
132	  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
133	- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
134	  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
135	- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
136	  in their stories, spec §8).
137	- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
138	  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).
139	
140	### Consequences
141	
142	- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
143	  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
144	- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
145	- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
146	  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
147	  code-backed rules.
148	- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
149	  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
150	- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
151	  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
152	  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
153	- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
154	  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
155	  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
156	- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
157	  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
158	- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
159	  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
160	- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
161	  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
162	- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
163	  HC1, US-01-Q-27).
164	
165	### Strongest argument against
166	
167	Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
168	scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
169	editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
170	needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
171	editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
172	country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
173	list would not.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
176	in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
177	country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
178	metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
179	duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
180	surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".
181	
182	### Confirmation
183	
184	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
185	  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
186	  (AC-22).
187	- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
188	  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
189	  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
190	- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
191	  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
192	  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
193	- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).
194	
195	## Pros and Cons of the Options
196	
197	### A. `country` collection type + relation
198	
199	- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
200	- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
201	- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
202	- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
203	- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.
204	
205	### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)
206	
207	Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).
208	
209	- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
210	  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
211	  per country with no custom code.
212	- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
213	- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
214	  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
215	  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
216	  price.
217	- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
218	  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
219	- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
220	  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.
221	
222	### C. Enumeration attribute `country`
223	
224	- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
225	- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
226	- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
227	  which BR-07 forbids.
228	
229	### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)
230	
231	- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
232	- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
233	  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
234	  without an extra flag).
235	- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
236	  error-prone for non-technical editors.
237	
238	### R1. Path segment (chosen)
239	
240	- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
241	- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
242	- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
243	  the other country's data).
244	
245	### R2. Host name
246	
247	- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
248	- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
249	  single-command start (Assessment, environment).
250	
251	### R3. Query parameter
252	
253	- Good, because it needs no routing change.
254	- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
255	  for guards and tests.
256	
257	### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser
258	
259	- Good, because URLs stay short.
260	- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
261	  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.
262	
263	## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)
264	
265	1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
266	   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
267	2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
268	   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
269	3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.
270	
271	## More Information
272	
273	- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
274	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
275	  (files cited inline).
276	- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
277	  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
278	- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
279	  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.
280

2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/utils, @strapi/admin, @strapi/plugin-users-permissions 5.63.0, Strapi REST docs (status parameter), Docker Official Image "nginx" docs
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
14	terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
15	(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
16	address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
17	how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the
18	browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: US-01-AC-27, US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16.
19	
20	## Decision Drivers
21	
22	- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3). Evaluated as "token and permission security" (source: Assessment, evaluation).
23	- D2. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07). The build must not embed an environment-specific API address.
24	- D3. "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." (source: Assessment); visible on the next full page load, no cache delaying it (US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16).
25	- D4. "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries" (source: Assessment, environment). Nothing may require a manual admin step to make the app work.
26	- D5. Drafts are never visible to end users (US-01-BR-06, US-01-AC-13).
27	- D6. AC-03 is automated: a test publishes a field during the run (US-01-Q-23), and the browser sees only GET requests without write tokens (US-01-AC-27).
28	- D7. Business editors use the Strapi admin, which must stay reachable (Assessment, business context).
29	
30	## Considered Options
31	
32	1. **Direct access with the public role**: the browser calls Strapi cross-origin with no token;
33	   the public role has `find`/`findOne` on the read types; the API URL comes from a runtime
34	   `config.json`.
35	2. **Same-origin nginx proxy + public role**: the nginx container that serves the Angular build
36	   forwards `GET /api/<allow-listed types>` to Strapi; the browser calls the relative path `/api`;
37	   Strapi's public role has only `find` on the read types and Strapi itself forces published
38	   content for anonymous requests.
39	3. **Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token**: the public role has no content
40	   permissions; nginx adds `Authorization: Bearer <read token>` to proxied requests; the token
41	   lives only in the proxy's environment.
42	
43	## Decision Outcome
44	
45	Chosen option: **"2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role"**, because it meets D1 with no token
46	anywhere near the browser and no secret to provision at start-up (D4), gives the same build a
47	relative API address that works in every environment (D2), and places the cache and method rules
48	in one small config file (D3, D6). The extra safeguard that matters most, forcing published
49	content, is enforced **inside Strapi**, so it holds even for requests that bypass the proxy (D5,
50	D7).
51	
52	### What is decided
53	
54	**Topology (docker compose)**
55	
56	- `frontend`: nginx (Docker Official Image) serving the Angular build on one origin, and proxying
57	  `/api/` to Strapi. The upstream address comes from an environment variable through the image's
58	  template mechanism (`/etc/nginx/templates/*.template` processed with `envsubst` into
59	  `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at container start; Docker Official Image "nginx" docs). The browser bundle
60	  contains no host name.
61	- `strapi`: exposes its own port for the admin panel used by editors (D7). The content API on that
62	  port is protected by the Strapi-side rules below, not by the proxy.
63	- Development (`ng serve`) uses the Angular dev-server proxy for `/api`, so the code path is the
64	  same relative URL. No `environment.ts` API URL, no runtime `config.json` (nothing to configure).
65	
66	**Proxy rules (nginx)**
67	
68	- Only `GET` (and the implicit `HEAD`) on an allow-list of paths: `/api/countries` and
69	  `/api/form-fields` in US-01; US-02 and US-03 add `/api/plans` and `/api/terms` through their
70	  specs. Any other method or path under `/api/` returns `405` or `404` without reaching Strapi.
71	- Responses under `/api/` carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; no `proxy_cache` is configured.
72	  `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; hashed build assets may be cached long-term
73	  (their names change on every build).
74	- Requests carrying an `Authorization` header are rejected (`400`), so the proxy can never be used
75	  to replay a token from a browser.
76	
77	**Strapi rules (bootstrap code, idempotent, applied on every start; no manual admin clicks)**
78	
79	- Public role: **exactly** `api::country.country.find` and `api::form-field.form-field.find` in
80	  US-01 (US-02 adds `api::plan.plan.find`, US-03 `api::terms.terms.find`). No `findOne`: the app
81	  never reads a single document by `documentId`. Justification per permission is in the table
82	  below. Bootstrap reconciles the role to this list (removes anything else) on every start.
83	- The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.callback`, `auth.connect`,
84	  `auth.forgotPassword`, `auth.resetPassword`, `auth.register`, `auth.emailConfirmation`,
85	  `auth.sendEmailConfirmation`, `auth.refresh`) are removed, and the advanced setting
86	  `allow_register` is set to `false`. Verified in `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`:
87	  `services/users-permissions.js` (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`) and `bootstrap/index.js`
88	  (`allow_register: true` by default). The app has no end-user accounts, so these endpoints are
89	  unneeded attack surface. Note: the plugin recreates its defaults only when the permissions table
90	  is empty (`syncPermissions`), which never happens while our `find` permissions exist.
91	- The authenticated role gets no content permissions.
92	- **Published only for anonymous reads.** The REST API accepts `status=draft` from any caller
93	  that has `find` (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `content-api-constants.js` lists `status` as an
94	  allowed query parameter; `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `core-api/service/core-service.js` defaults it to
95	  `published` only when absent; the Strapi REST docs page on `status` states no permission
96	  requirement for `status=draft`). With a plain public `find`, anyone could read drafts with
97	  `?status=draft`. A Strapi global middleware therefore removes `status`, `publicationFilter` and
98	  `hasPublishedVersion` from content API requests that are not authenticated by an API token, so
99	  the default (`published`) always applies to anonymous reads.
100	- CORS (`strapi::cors`, default `origin: '*'` in `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `middlewares/cors.js`) is
101	  restricted to an environment-driven allow-list, empty by default: the browser reaches the
102	  content API same-origin through nginx and never needs CORS.
103	- Strapi creates a default "Full Access" API token on a fresh database with no admin user and no
104	  token (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `bootstrap.js`, `createDefaultAPITokensIfNeeded`). It never
105	  reaches the browser, but it is an unused write credential: bootstrap deletes the default
106	  "Full Access" token, and it is never copied into any `.env`.
107	
108	| Public permission | Why it is needed | Data exposed |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| `api::country.country.find` | Chooser, unknown-country links, currency and locale (ADR-0001); required by Strapi to filter `form-field` by `country.code` | Country code, name, currency, locale. Public by nature. |
111	| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Step 1 form (US-01-BR-01) | Labels, rules, options, Spanish copy. Public by nature (shown to every visitor). |
112	
113	**Caching**
114	
115	- No HTTP cache interceptor and no service worker caching of `/api/` in Angular; content is loaded
116	  once per full page load and held in memory (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001).
117	- No Strapi REST cache plugin. Strapi 5.63.0 core sets no `Cache-Control` on content API
118	  responses (no occurrence in `@strapi/core@5.63.0/dist`); nginx adds `no-store`.
119	
120	**End-to-end writes for AC-03 (US-01-Q-23)**
121	
122	- The write credential exists only in the **Playwright Node process**. Flow:
123	  1. Bootstrap creates a development super admin from `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` /
124	     `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when no admin user exists (fictitious values in `.env.example`; real
125	     `.env` git-ignored). The human uses the same account at HC3.
126	  2. The test's setup logs in to the admin API (`POST /admin/login`, verified in
127	     `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `routes/authentication.js`; the response includes an access token)
128	     directly against Strapi's port, not through nginx.
129	  3. It creates a **custom** API token (`POST /admin/api-tokens`, type `custom`, verified in
130	     `routes/api-tokens.js` and `services/constants.js`: types `read-only`, `full-access`,
131	     `custom`) scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`, with the shortest
132	     lifespan Strapi accepts (7 days; the validator accepts only `null`, 7, 30 or 90 days).
133	  4. It creates the `mobilePhone` field with `POST /api/form-fields` on Strapi's port. A REST
134	     `POST` publishes immediately unless `status=draft` is passed (Strapi REST docs, `status`
135	     page), which is what AC-03 needs.
136	  5. Teardown deletes the field and then the token (`DELETE /admin/api-tokens/:id`), also when the
137	     test fails.
138	- The token and the admin JWT are never passed to `page.evaluate`, `page.route`,
139	  `addInitScript`, cookies or storage of the browser context. The browser under test talks only to
140	  nginx, which rejects any `Authorization` header and any non-GET method.
141	
142	### Consequences
143	
144	- Good, because no token of any kind is ever sent by the browser or stored on disk by the app (D1).
145	- Good, because the same build runs in compose, in `ng serve` and in any future host: the API path
146	  is relative (D2).
147	- Good, because drafts stay unreadable even when someone calls Strapi's port directly with
148	  `?status=draft` (D5).
149	- Good, because one start command is enough: no token has to be generated and copied before the
150	  front end works (D4).
151	- Bad, because anyone who can reach Strapi's port can call the two public `find` endpoints
152	  directly, bypassing the proxy's allow-list — mitigation: the data is public by nature, drafts are
153	  blocked in Strapi, and the role has no other permission. Rate limiting is out of scope.
154	- Bad, because the published-only rule is custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade could make
155	  incomplete (for example a new publication query parameter) — mitigation: an automated check
156	  (below) requests the seeded draft field anonymously; re-verify on every Strapi upgrade.
157	- Bad, because the e2e setup depends on Strapi's admin API (`/admin/login`, `/admin/api-tokens`),
158	  which is what the admin panel uses but is less documented than the REST API — mitigation: it is
159	  used only by tests; if it changes, only the AC-03 test breaks, and the HC3 manual check of AC-03
160	  in the admin remains.
161	- Bad, because a development admin account is created from environment variables — mitigation:
162	  fictitious values only in `.env.example`, `.env` git-ignored, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh`.
163	- Neutral: nginx is needed anyway to serve the Angular build; the proxy adds a few lines of
164	  configuration, not a new service.
165	
166	### Strongest argument against
167	
168	Strapi's own port, which stays open for the admin panel, still answers the public `find`
169	endpoints to anyone who can reach it, and those requests skip the proxy's method and path
170	allow-list entirely. On that port, keeping drafts hidden rests only on custom published-only
171	middleware, which a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete (for example through a new
172	publication query parameter) without any error. Option 3 (proxy-injected read-only token, empty
173	public role) would close Strapi's port to anonymous content reads altogether.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** the two exposed endpoints serve data that is public by nature, and the
176	public role has no other permission. Option 3 needs the token to exist before nginx starts,
177	which breaks the single start command (D4), and it gives the browser the same effective access
178	through the proxy, so its gain is limited to the direct port. The draft rule is guarded by an
179	automated anonymous request for the seeded draft field, re-run on every Strapi upgrade.
180	
181	### Confirmation
182	
183	- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
184	  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
185	- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
186	  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
187	  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
188	- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
189	  token is created and deleted in Node only.
190	- Review checklist: bootstrap reconciles the public role to the table above; `allow_register` is
191	  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
192	  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
193	
194	## Pros and Cons of the Options
195	
196	### 1. Direct access with the public role
197	
198	- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
199	- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
200	  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
201	  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
202	- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
203	- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.
204	
205	### 2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role (chosen)
206	
207	- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
208	- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.
209	- Good, because method, path and cache rules sit in one reviewed file.
210	- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).
211	
212	### 3. Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token
213	
214	- Good, because the public role can be empty: Strapi's port answers `403` to anonymous content
215	  requests.
216	- Bad, because the token must exist before nginx starts: Strapi generates the key randomly at
217	  creation (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `services/api-token.js`, `crypto.randomBytes`), so a single
218	  `docker compose up` would need Strapi to write the secret to a shared volume or to insert a
219	  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).
220	- Bad, because the `read-only` type grants `find`/`findOne` on **every** content type, including
221	  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
222	  published-only rule is still needed.
223	- Bad, because the proxy then grants anyone who reaches it the token's rights, so the browser's
224	  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.
225	
226	## More Information
227	
228	- Verified sources (2026-11-20; packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
229	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@strapi/admin@5.63.0`,
230	  `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`, `@angular/core@22.3.0` (files cited inline);
231	  https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status (REST default `published`, `POST`/`PUT` publish
232	  unless `status=draft`); https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx (environment variables via templates).
233	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
234	  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
235	- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
236	  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
237	  reading drafts through the content API.
238

consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/utils, @strapi/admin, @strapi/plugin-users-permissions 5.63.0, Strapi REST docs (status parameter), Docker Official Image "nginx" docs
